findings.title: Routine cleanup logs use Error level
findings.body: The new cleanup paths emit r.log.Error for normal, expected operations: 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time', 'Annotations to clean by count', 'cleaned annotations by count', 'Tags to clean', 'cleaned tags' (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). These are routine successful operations that will fire on every cleanup cycle. With the cleanup ticker in cleanup.go now firing every minute (a separate change in this PR), this produces a steady stream of Error-level log entries masking real errors. Severity is amplified by the same PR also logging all IDs ('ids', ids), which can be up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries (up to 32767) per batch, potentially producing enormous log lines. These should be Debug/Info level, not Error.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker shortened 10x without justification
findings.body: Ticker changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`. The PR description is solely about fixing a MySQL deadlock via query restructuring; nothing in the description or the referenced issue (grafana/grafana#64979) justifies a 10x increase in cleanup frequency. This multiplies the database load of every cleanup job by 10x, including annotation cleanup, dashboard version cleanup, short URL cleanup, query history cleanup, etc. Combined with the noisy Error logs added in xorm_store.go, this materially changes operational behavior and should either be split into its own change or justified explicitly. Note also that `cleanUpOldAnnotations` is called inside this 1-minute loop, and the new fetch+delete implementation uses two round-trips per batch instead of one, compounding the load.

findings.title: O(N^2) string building in SQLite IN-list inlining
SQLite parameter-limit branch checks config, not actual ID count
findings.body: The branch `if r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` decides whether to inline IDs into the SQL based on the configured batch size, not on `len(ids)`. The actual number of parameters needed equals `len(ids)`, which is bounded by `LIMIT AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` but usually far smaller (cleanup often finds only a handful of rows). When the operator sets a large batch size (e.g., the new test exercises 32767), the inlining path is taken on every call even if only a few rows are being deleted, building a needless literal string and skipping the (correct) parameterized path. Use `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`.

findings.title: Log fields include 'err' even when fetch succeeded
findings.body: Each new cleanup log line passes `"err", err` as a structured field. The `err` here is the result of `fetchIDs`, which is nil on the success path. Every successful cleanup therefore emits `"err": <nil>` in its log payload, which is misleading to operators triaging errors (especially since these are emitted at Error level - see the other finding). The 'err' field should only be included when err is non-nil, or the message should be split so success and failure paths log different things.
